public_rationale: In his September 7, 2023 interview, Hoffman predicted human-expert hallucination rates “within months.” [e4] Research revised on February 21, 2024 found hallucinations in most evaluated ChatGPT and Llama2-Chat outputs in information-seeking scenarios, but did not compare their error rates with those of experts answering equivalent questions. [e5] These sources do not establish whether systems available by March 31, 2024 had reached human-expert factual reliability. [e4, e5]
limitations: The interview identifies the hallucination prediction but does not establish the complete set of predictions Marcus referenced. [e4]

from_speaker: have not thus far borne out
our_interpretation: The referenced TIME interview contains Hoffman's prediction that hallucination rates could reach human-expert rates within months.
The following paragraph about hallucinations makes that prediction the clearest identifiable referent. The supplied text does not establish every prediction contained in the embedded material.
I assess whether that capability had materialized by March 31, 2024. I do not treat the statement as saying that every possible interpretation of Hoffman's deadline had expired.
Human-expert parity means comparable factual reliability on representative tasks under comparable conditions, rather than merely passing an examination or improving over an earlier model.

criteria.contradiction_condition: A credible comparison establishes that a system available by March 31, 2024 had reached the referenced human-expert hallucination rate across the relevant factual tasks.
